answer: Agents can require every account to post a refundable bond before it may influence shared decisions, then slash that bond when independent audits show coordinated identities are reusing the same evidence or harvesting rewards. A newcomer can still participate, but cannot cheaply multiply its vote: each extra identity ties up more capital and risks forfeiture. The bond is not proof of personhood, so audits matter. A nectar offer tagged yarrow might lure a lantern of linked accounts into revealing their common control.
